Passengers should follow all commands and
signals given by crewmembers. Be ready to
assist crewmembers in an emergency and to
follow the guidelines below:
1) Know where all the exits are on this aircraft.
Study the briefing card and know how to
open the

TO SIT IN AN EXIT ROW
In order to ensure the fastest possible
emergency evacuation, the Federal Aviation
Administration has set standards for people who
sit in rows next to exits. In the event of an
emergency, these passengers may be called
upon to assist crewmembers in the evacuation..
Passengers sitting in exit row seats must be
willing and able to do the following:
1) Locate the emergency exit and move quickly
to it;
2) Recognize the opening
mechanism,
comprehend the instructions, then open the
exit at the proper time;
3) Decide if opening the exit will increase
hazards to passengers;
4) Follow instructions given by crewmembers;
5)
Stow the exit doors;
6)
Pass quickly through the door and then
assess, select and follow a safe path away
from the aircraft.
In order to perform all of these functions,
passengers sitting in emergency exit rows
must:
1) Read English well enough to understand the
instructions for opening exits and for other
emergency procedures.
2)
See well enough to read instructions, to see
signals given by crewmembers and to look
outside for dangers such as smoke, fire or
water which would make the exit unusable.
You can wear glasses or contact lenses;
3)
Hear well enough to understand English
commands. You can use a hearing aid;
4)
Speak well enough to give information in
English to
crewmembers
or other
passengers during an emergency;
5) Be able to use both hands, both arms and
both legs, as well as be strong and flexible
enough to do the following:
a. Be able to quickly open the exit. This will
require that you be able to reach up,
sideways and down and be able to grasp
the door mechanism;
Be able to lift the exit door out of the exit;
some window hatches that must be lifted
can weigh as much as 65 pounds (30
Kgs.), the average weight of a 7 year old
child;
Be able to clear from the exit any
obstructions weighing up to 65 pounds
and to maintain balance while doing so;
d. Be able to quickly move to and through
the exit;
e. Be able to help other passengers away
from the plane;
6) Be at least 15 years of age;
7) Have the capacity to perform these functions
without a companion or adult;
8) Be with no one that requires your care, such
as a small child, or someone physically or
mentally unable to care for themselves;
9) You must be willing and able to do all of
these things by yourself and without harming
yourself.
If you cannot or do not wish to do all these
things, you cannot sit in an emergency exit
row seat. If you are already seated there, ask
a crewmember to move you to another seat.
You do not have to explain why. You need to
say only "I do not want to sit in an exit row."
